messages:
anna: Heads-up: canary run after the kernel-selector change shows a ~12-18% p95 token latency regression on long seqs (4096). Reproducible on prod-like traces.
kevin: ugh. which change exactly? commit?
jordan: commit 9f3b2c4 — heuristics for kernel preference based on warmup/kv-hit-rate.
anna: yep that one. baseline (before) -> after: p50 ~same, p95 jump. throughput unchanged.
miguel: can you share an nsys capture?
anna: uploaded nsys here: https://internal-artifacts/runs/3543219876/nsys.zip. Quick note: I captured two runs back-to-back (before/after) with --capture-range=timestamp.
perf-bot: nsys capture archived: run_id=3543219876, objects=runtime,kv-cache,batcher.
kevin: quick look at the flame shows extra memcpy spikes right before kernel launch in the after trace. Could be KV eviction touching pages.
jordan: interesting — the kernel selector started preferring kernel-B for high-kv-hit paths, which adds a short memcpy for prefetched KV blocks. Might be more frequent now due to changed warmup threshold.
anna: snippet from perfetto timeline (after):
```
[...hot timeline excerpt...]
Memcpy H2D 12.4ms
Memory touch 2.1ms
Kernel-B launch 1.6ms
KV lookup 0.3ms
```
kevin: compare to before: Memcpy 0.4ms, Kernel-A launch 2.0ms. So total token critical path increased.
miguel: maybe memcpy is coming from the new prefetch that does a synchronous copy when it misses in the compact cache path. Should be async ideally.
jordan: I ran an nvprof-like command and saw increased PCIe memcpy calls on the hot path: `nvprof --trace-memcpy`.
anna: I bisected across 20 commits and narrowed to 9f3b2c4 -> toggling the warmup threshold back fixes p95 in canary. Bisect notes: http://ci/bisect/3543.
kevin: good. Can we tweak kernel selector to avoid forcing kernel-B for sequences with >X cold kv misses? We should prefer kernel-A until prefetch is warmed.
miguel: quick patch idea: make kernel preference probabilistic during warmup window (50% kernel-A), or make prefetch async+copy deferred. I can prototype async prefetch.
jordan: also worth checking batcher handoff—if kernel choice causes more batch splits, head-of-line scheduling can amplify latency. I saw a few 1-item batches in the after trace.
anna: reproducer script I used: `tools/repro/trace_repro.sh --model=gpt-like --seq=4096 --requests=2000 --nsys` (linked in artifact).
kevin: next steps: miguel prototype async prefetch, anna run canary with selector toggled to prefer kernel-A, jordan inspect batcher thresholds for 1-item splits.
anna: assigned. adding label perf/regression and scheduling a quick sync in 30m. :calendar:
perf-bot: ticket created PERF-8792 for investigation, estimate 3d.
kevin: if we can avoid sync memcpy on critical path we should be able to recover p95. thanks team.
